title: FBI opens national security investigation into John Lennon | 1972
content:
The FBI opened its investigation into John Lennon on 21 January 1972.

The Federal Bureau of Investigation had been aware of Lennon’s political activism for some time, which had grown since his relocation to New York City in August 1971.

Lennon was believed to be funding what the FBI termed the Allamuchy Tribe, a protest group run by former members of the Chicago Seven, who had been charged with various counterculture offences during the 1968 Democratic National Convention.

Lennon had donated $75,000 to the group, and met its members Jerry Rubin and Abbie Hoffman on a number of occasions. They were termed the Allamuchy Tribe as a result of its meetings in Alamuchy, New Jersey.

3 FEB 1972

SUBJECT: John LENNON;
Allamuchy Tribe (NL)

1. Reference is made to your teletype 003, dated 24 January 1972, Subject: Protest Activity and Civil Disturbances, reporting that former Beatles singer John LENNON had contributed a large sum of money to the “Allamuchy Tribe”, headed by Rennie DAVIS.

2. It is requested that you furnish this office with any additional pertinent information concerning LENNON’S relationship with the “Allamuchy Tribe” and any indications that DAVIS has received other funds for his activities from foreign sources.

FBI memo, 3 February 1972

The FBI file on Lennon was closed on 8 December 1972.
